newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says alerted on Versace suspect in May.
newsitem.headline: Manila says alerted on Versace suspect in May.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation alerted Manila as early as May to look out for a man it has named as the suspected killer of fashion king Gianni Versace, officials said on Wednesday.

Philippine National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) director Santiago Toledo said the family of the suspect, Andrew Cunanan, 27, had roots in the towns of Malolos and Baliuag in Bulacan province, near Manila, but declined to give details.
Cunanan is a Filipino name but NBI officials said they had no information on his family's background.
Toledo told reporters the NBI placed Cunanan on its watch list after it received the FBI alert in May describing Cunanan as extremely dangerous.
NBI investigations revealed that Cunanan, an American citizen, came to the Philippines in December 1988 in his only known visit to this country, Toledo said.
Versace, 50, died on Tuesday after being shot twice in the head at the gates of his Miami Beach mansion.
Miami Beach police chief Richard Barreto told reporters that Cunanan, whom he described as a male prostitute, was their only suspect.

U.S. investigators have described Cunanan as an alleged serial killer suspected of four murders, including that of his former male lover during a two-week, cross-country killing spree that began in Minneapolis.
